statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of six representative public paths. Authenticated betting, deposit, cancellation and post-registration form submission were not covered because no account or financial transaction was used.

page.framework: server-rendered multi-page application with legacy Java/JSP-style routes and mixed modern/legacy templates
page.notes: Japanese mobile-oriented wagering and race-information service. Representative set covers global home, sport landing, race list, article, registration entry and 404 recovery. Not covered: authenticated betting/deposit/account flows, destructive or financial actions, all sport variants and every campaign page because they either require credentials/risk real transactions or duplicate sampled templates.

paths.description: Homepage and primary betting/navigation hub; represents global chrome, campaigns, live status and main calls to action.
Horse-racing section landing page; represents a sport listing/index template.
Daily race list; represents transactional race information and repeated action controls.
Service notice article; represents public editorial/content detail pages and no-JS delivery.
New-member registration entry; represents the primary account acquisition journey. The first choice was activated and revealed bank-registration options.
Deliberately invalid URL; exercises HTTP failure messaging and recovery links.

findings.summary: The interface does not adapt to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark/reduced-motion screenshot is visually identical to the light rendering, and the rendered CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme or color-scheme declaration on the main templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define tested dark surface, text, border and image treatments with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Contrast preferences are not explicitly supported and baseline contrast already fails.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors treatment; axe found 18 color-contrast failures on the homepage and 3 on registration.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix WCAG contrast failures first, then preserve system colors/outlines and test controls under forced-colors and prefers-contrast.

findings.summary: Major route and state changes are abrupt.
findings.evidence: Across the homepage, listing, race, article and registration probes, no authored View Transition treatment was found and navigation is full-page/instant.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained same-document or cross-document view transitions for meaningful route/state continuity, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome overwhelms task content on the primary entry pages.
findings.evidence: The homepage and horse-racing screenshots devote the first several viewports to registration and rotating campaign artwork before race/task information; 61 images and a 3,988px mobile page reinforce the density.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce and prioritise campaigns, expose the current race/task state earlier, and defer below-fold campaign rendering.

findings.summary: A primary registration button has no visible keyboard focus indicator.
findings.evidence: The active-element probe focused “口座振替をして会員登録” and computed outline: none with no box-shadow, while the homepage anchor retained a browser outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator to every custom button/link and verify the full registration path by keyboard.

findings.summary: The 404 recovery page sends users to insecure legacy URLs.
findings.evidence: The invalid-path probe showed a clear Japanese error but every recovery link targets http://m.oddspark.com rather than the current HTTPS site, and there is no h1.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a proper 404 page in the current responsive shell with HTTPS recovery links, a heading, search/home actions and preserved navigation.

findings.summary: The homepage’s Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10,526ms (performance score 0.57); the independent trace measured LCP 10,346ms and FCP 7,338ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the LCP element, make it discoverable in initial HTML, prioritise only that asset, reduce server/critical-chain delay and retest under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The homepage shifts visibly during load.
findings.evidence: Layout observation measured CLS 0.111 mobile and 0.166 desktop; Lighthouse corroborated CLS 0.118. The image audit found 39 images without dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve intrinsic image/banner space with width/height or aspect-ratio and prevent late campaign/widget insertion from moving existing content.

findings.summary: The homepage ships an excessive, poorly optimised resource payload.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 146 requests and 6.40MB transferred, including 4.21MB images and 2.04MB scripts. The image audit found 53 legacy-format images, 30 without srcset and 19 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive AVIF/WebP sources, lazy-load below-fold campaigns, set dimensions, consolidate requests and preserve eager/high-priority loading only for the LCP image.

findings.summary: Script execution and unused code add avoidable main-thread cost.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 327.5ms TBT, 2.91s main-thread work, 1.74s boot-up time and about 826KB potential unused JavaScript savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused tags/libraries, load non-critical dependencies conditionally, and break or schedule remaining long work.

findings.summary: Key controls and embedded content lack valid accessible names/roles.
findings.evidence: axe found critical ARIA parent errors, invalid roles, four unnamed homepage links, an untitled chat iframe, and an unnamed registration link; the image probe also found 17 images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native elements/valid ARIA ownership, add meaningful link and iframe names, and provide purposeful alt text or empty alt for decoration.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: axe identified 18 homepage and 3 registration contrast violations, including section headings, race status text and primary registration controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state and verify both default and forced-colors modes.

findings.summary: Landmark and heading structure is inconsistent across templates.
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark and 48 homepage regions outside landmarks. Probes showed duplicate h1 elements and many empty h3 elements; registration also lacks a main landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce header/nav/main/footer landmarks, one descriptive h1 per page and a logical non-empty heading hierarchy.

findings.summary: Every representative template disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: The homepage, section, race and article viewport meta use user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1; axe rates the homepage and registration instance critical.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and restrictive maximum-scale/minimum-scale values, then verify 200% and 400% zoom/reflow.

findings.summary: A third-party analytics request produces console errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a Yahoo analytics fetch blocked by CORS plus ERR_FAILED during homepage load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or correct the failing tag/request and configure third-party telemetry so failures do not pollute runtime diagnostics.

findings.summary: Public pages omit meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: Rendered probes found no meta description on the homepage, horse-racing landing, race list or service notice, despite useful titles and crawlable content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add concise, page-specific meta descriptions to each public template.

findings.summary: Important controls use non-crawlable JavaScript links.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found JavaScript URLs and Lighthouse crawlable-anchors failed; examples include menu, login, “all” and voting controls represented as javascript: links.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for in-page actions and real href URLs for navigation, preserving progressive enhancement and crawler-visible destinations.

findings.summary: Public content has no structured or social metadata.
findings.evidence: The homepage, section, race and article probes found zero JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags; registration is the only sampled surface with partial OG metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite and page-specific structured data plus canonical Open Graph/Twitter fields for shareable public content.

findings.summary: The main document lacks baseline defensive security headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. HTTPS itself is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP in report-only then enforced mode, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, a restrictive referrer policy and least-privilege permissions policy.

findings.summary: The homepage has a disproportionate tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker capture observed 35 third-party origins and known Google Tag Manager, Facebook and DoubleClick trackers; HAR recorded 146 requests. No consent surface appeared in the captured first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and justify each third party, remove redundant trackers, defer optional analytics until consent/context, and minimise collected identifiers and retention.

findings.summary: Most cookies are sent without Secure and with permissive SameSite settings.
findings.evidence: The cookie audit found 20 cookies, 20 counted insecure; numerous analytics/identifier cookies lack Secure, use SameSite=None and persist for 390–400 days. Session cookies were HttpOnly but still SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is necessary, shorten identifier lifetimes and keep auth/session cookies HttpOnly.

findings.summary: The sampled account entry does not expose a modern authentication option.
findings.evidence: The public login/registration surfaces showed conventional login/registration controls but no WebAuthn/passkey capability or contextual credential flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys alongside existing methods, with user-initiated registration, authentication, recovery and management flows.

findings.summary: Public race and service content has no offline/installable support.
findings.evidence: All probes found no manifest, no controlling service worker and no installability surface, although the site provides time-sensitive but reusable race/content pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a manifest and service worker with an offline shell/fallback and cache safe public content; keep transactional betting network-required with explicit offline messaging.

findings.summary: Core landing pages omit the document language.
findings.evidence: The homepage and horse-racing landing probes returned an empty html lang; race, article and registration templates correctly use lang=ja.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang=ja consistently at the template root and retain correct language changes for embedded multilingual content.

findings.summary: Campaign imagery is not delivered sustainably.
findings.evidence: The image audit found no modern-format images among 61 sampled, 53 legacy images, 30 missing responsive sources, 19 below-fold images loaded eagerly and 5 oversized assets; images transfer 4.21MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, use picture/srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold media and enforce a per-template image budget.

taskList.title: Restore zoom, keyboard focus and accessibility semantics
Cut homepage LCP, payload and campaign cost
Deploy defensive headers and secure cookie defaults
Reduce and consent-gate the tracking stack
Rebuild the 404 recovery surface with HTTPS links
Prioritise task content over promotional chrome
Repair discoverability metadata and crawlable controls
Set lang consistently and remove console failures
